title.title: Saxl's conjecture: the staircase tensor square has everything
title.subtitle: Claim: the tensor square of the staircase representation of $S_n$ contains every irreducible

plain: Squaring one staircase-shaped symmetry pattern produces every other pattern at least once

beats.text: Its Specht module $S^{\rho_m}$ is one irreducible representation of $S_n$
Saxl: its tensor square contains every irreducible, so every Kronecker coefficient is positive

steps: For each target shape, write down one explicit vector
Each vector lies in one cyclic piece of the tensor square
It generates a copy of its target: every one appears

achievement.label: Saxl's conjecture (2012)
achievement.context: Before: hooks and two-row shapes (Pak–Panova–Vallejo), shapes comparable with $\rho_m$ (Ikenmeyer)
achievement.note: Companion: every $n$ outside $\{2,4,9\}$ has a universal tensor square

voice.text: Saxl said the tensor square of the staircase representation contains every irreducible.
For each target, an explicit vector in one cyclic piece generates a copy.
Claimed: every Kronecker coefficient here is strictly positive.

sources.quote: Saxl conjectured in 2012 that the tensor square of the staircase representation of $S_n$, for $n=m(m+1)/2$ and shape $(m,m-1,\dots,1)$, contains every irreducible representation
Pak, Panova and Vallejo proved hooks and two-row shapes for large $m$, and Ikenmeyer proved shapes comparable with $\rho_m$ in dominance order.
for every $n$ outside $\{2,4,9\}$, some irreducible of $S_n$ has a universal tensor square
The stronger single-cyclic-vector statement is not.
